description: I am a Computer Science and Engineering student interested in software development, space science, and innovative technology. I am developing Earth Jukebox for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, an application that transforms NASA Earth science data into meaningful sounds to make science more accessible, especially for visually impaired people. I welcome passionate collaborators with skills in programming, Python, web development, Earth science, music, audio engineering, or UI/UX design.
summary:
Earth Jukebox is an accessible web application that transforms NASA Earth observations and climate records into synchronized musical soundscapes. Modeled on NASA’s Caldwell 73 sonification principles, it pairs live NASA GISS global surface temperature anomalies (1880–present) with NASA GIBS and Worldview satellite imagery—covering land temperature, ocean gradients, forest vegetation, atmospheric aerosols, and nighttime lights—plus an importer for downloaded NASA Earth Information Center and Scientific Visualization Studio frames.
Using real-time pixel analysis and dynamic audio synthesis, Earth Jukebox converts measured warming and thermal colors into pitch, brightness into volume, East–West distribution into stereo panning, and frame changes into rhythm. Listeners can toggle between Scientific Mode for consistent precision and Artistic Mode for expressive soundscapes, supported by plain-English explanations, keyboard shortcuts, screen-reader announcements, optional spoken narration, and a High-Contrast theme.
By turning sight-dependent planetary data into sound, Earth Jukebox makes Earth science accessible and engaging for blind, low-vision, and sighted audiences alike.
details:
What Earth Jukebox Does & How It Works Earth Jukebox (Hear the Earth. Understand the Change.) is an accessible, interactive web application that transforms genuine NASA Earth observations and climate records into synchronized, meaningful musical soundscapes. The application operates through a real-time four-stage pipeline: Official NASA Data Retrieval: A lightweight proxy server fetches live NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4) numerical anomalies (1880–present) and NASA GIBS / Worldview Snapshots satellite imagery across five Earth science datasets—Global Temperature Changes (MODIS_Terra_Land_Surface_Temp_Day), Ocean Currents & Thermal Gradients (GHRSST_L4_MUR_Sea_Surface_Temperature), Forest Coverage & Vegetation Pulse (MODIS_Terra_NDVI_8Day), Atmospheric Aerosols (OMPS_Aerosol_Index), and Earth at Night (VIIRS_Black_Marble). Users can also upload downloaded PNG/JPG image sequences from the NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) (such as Perpetual Ocean 2, GEOS Aerosols, DYAMOND CO₂, ISS Lightning Events, or GEDI Forest Height). Computer Vision & Scientific Analysis: An HTML5 Canvas analyzer extracts Red, Green, and Blue color intensities, perceived luminosity, East–West spatial center-of-mass, coverage, 8 longitudinal energy bands, and frame-to-frame changes. When measured scientific data is available (such as GISTEMP °C anomalies), the engine prioritizes exact numerical measurements over visual color estimates. Configurable Sonification Engine: Modeled after NASA’s Caldwell 73 sonification principles, extracted metrics drive real-time Web Audio synthesis: higher temperatures and warm red intensity raise musical pitch, cooler baselines and blue zones lower pitch, brightness controls volume, East–West spatial distribution controls stereo panning, and frame-to-frame changes modulate rhythm and tempo (BPM). Synchronized Studio Player: Displays the visualization alongside an interactive timeline scrubber, a live audio waveform and tabular telemetry bar, a hover Lat/Lon/RGB probe, and an Understand the Sound guide explaining what every sound represents. Benefits & Intended Impact Breaking Accessibility Barriers: Most climate visualizations rely exclusively on sight. Earth Jukebox makes planetary change audible and navigable for blind and low-vision users through aria-live announcements, full keyboard shortcuts (Space, S, ←/→, M, H), plain-English frame descriptions, optional spoken audio narration, and a dedicated High-Contrast display theme. Intuitive Climate Storytelling: Hearing 146 years of NASA GISTEMP global temperature anomalies climb from low, calm 19th-century bass notes into bright, rapid modern pitches communicates the pace of climate change emotionally and immediately—useful for classrooms, museums, outreach, and public education. Scientific Transparency: Every dataset clearly distinguishes between directly measured scientific data (°C anomalies) and image-derived color/brightness proxies so users understand both the insights and limitations of visual sonification.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS Frontend & Visualization: React, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 2D Canvas (pixel-level computer vision analysis), SVG data visualization, Web Speech API (optional spoken narration) Audio Synthesis: Tone.js and the browser Web Audio API (multi-voice synthesis, stereo panning, harmonic scales, and real-time waveform/FFT analysis) Backend Proxy & Build Tooling: Node.js, Express (CORS-clean caching proxy for NASA APIs), Vite Official NASA Data Sources: NASA GISS (GISTEMP v4), NASA GIBS / Worldview Snapshots API, NASA JPL PO.DAAC, NASA LP DAAC, NASA Suomi NPP OMPS, and NASA EIC / SVS conceptual resources

How the Project Is Creative Dual Listening Modes: Users can switch instantaneously between Scientific Mode (a dry, calibrated triangle-wave signal with optional continuous Chromatic Hz output for analytical repeatability) and Artistic Mode (expressive harmonic pad chords, 8-band longitudinal FM melodic sweeps, and bright-spike shimmers that preserve the exact underlying data trends). Interactive Crosshair Spatial Probe: Hovering over any satellite map samples exact Latitude, Longitude, RGB values, and local luminosity in real time. Bring-Your-Own NASA SVS Frames: Beyond the 5 live datasets, the built-in frame importer turns any downloaded NASA SVS animation sequence into an instant musical instrument. Key Factors Considered Accessibility First: Designing controls that work seamlessly without sight (semantic landmarks, ≥44px touch targets, reduced-motion support, keyboard-only playback, and spoken summaries). Scientific Honesty: Prioritizing numerical °C records over approximate pixel colors and explicitly documenting color-palette limitations inside the Understand the Sound section. Reliability for Live Demos: Caching NASA API responses in the Express proxy with an offline GISTEMP backup ensures smooth, lag-free playback even on slow connections. Pleasant, Understandable Audio: Mapping values onto curated musical scales (Pentatonic Major, Lydian, Dorian, Natural Minor, Chromatic) so data trends sound musical and distinguishable rather than harsh random noise.
